$doc: THE INK-DESIGN REGISTRY — the second layer of a reverse holo.
A reverse holo is TWO orthogonal things, and the 43-type foil taxonomy conflates them:
FOIL    embossed micro-texture in aluminium. Physical, so a procedural GLSL recipe is
the correct model and packages/patterns is the correct home. This registry does
not touch it.
DESIGN  opaque ink printed OVER that sheet, blocking it. An artist's layout from TPCi.
Procedural will never converge on it BECAUSE THERE IS NOTHING TO CONVERGE TO:
Sceptile and Magneton, and a dozen other visually different reverses, sit on the
SAME vertical-sheen sheet. So the design is data, and this file is the data.
KEYING is (scope, type, variantKind), resolving card > subset > set > era, with RARITY
joining the key because the EX era gates ink on it (gold name, gold HP, silver rarity
symbol, per set and in one set per card). It is deliberately NOT (era, type): Prismatic
Evolutions ships three different reverses of the SAME card on the same sheet, Black Bolt
and White Flare do the same, Ascended Heroes carries six, and the Plasma sets substitute
a Team Plasma shield for the type symbol on Team Plasma cards only. Every one of those is
invisible to a key without variantKind.
ONE TILE PLUS PLACEMENT, never a card-sized raster. Overprints are periodic: a tile and
six numbers are a few KB and scale by construction, where a per-card raster is a corpus
that grows with the catalog and can never be finished.
AN EMPTY `tile` IS A REAL STATE, not a gap. Recognisable marks — Poke Ball, Master Ball,
the Team Plasma insignia, the energy symbols — are TPCi's designs and may not be traced
into a CC0 corpus (AGENTS.md F2). Those rows keep their measured placement and leave the
slot empty: uInkOn stays 0 for that key, the recipe renders its procedural fallback
exactly as it does today, and the work appears on the task queue with the ownership
caution attached. See data/ink-tiles/INK-TILES-NOTICE.md and `queued` below.
GENERATED INDEX: tools/build-ink-index.mjs trims this into packages/resolver/src/
ink-index.json, which is what @foilkit/resolver bundles. Edit THIS file; regenerate that
one. CI runs the builder with --check.
source: 3b (holo-archive/3b-pairs: delta-classes.md, era-research.md) for the delta classes and the keying evidence; the period measurement in `tiles[].period` is this subtask's own and is weak — see its `n`.

$doc: PER-FRAME-RECORD OVERRIDE on data/frames.json's `shows`.
frames.json says `shows` is `unknown` on every one of its 24 records, and its own $doc is
explicit that this is the finding rather than a gap: derived, never claimed, and `unknown`
means NO CLAIM. It also sets the rule this compositor obeys — only a MEASURED `reverse`
may suppress an overlay.
THE DEFAULT IS THEREFORE `normal`, AND IT IS AN ASSUMPTION, stated here so it can be
argued with: every catalog scan is the normal printing, per the TCGdex convention that one
image serves every variant of a card. This subtask measured it on n = 7 catalog scans
(autocorrelation of the sheet band, peak SNR 1.41-1.88 against a validated positive
control at 7.85) and found no printed design in any of them, INCLUDING two cards with no
non-reverse printing at all. The assumption held on everything measured. It is still an
assumption.
This map is the escape hatch, and it is a HUMAN ratchet (AGENTS.md F4): a frame id here
with the value `reverse` sets uInkDraw 0 for every card resolved through that frame, and
no regeneration may remove it. Empty today, honestly — nothing has been measured to
`reverse`, and inventing an entry would be exactly the claim frames.json refuses to make.

dot-grid.geometry: one centred disc, r = 38% of the cell

period.method: autocorrelation of high-passed luma over the sheet band (canonical px 60-444 x 380-590), strongest design-scale x peak at lag 43 px -> 504/43 = 11.7 tiles across the card width
period.caveat: One peak, on one of four photographed pairs, at SNR 2.1. 3b records those pairs as misregistered (band-pass NCC 0.10-0.34 on three of four) and the sheet band contains the text box, which has a line rhythm of its own. This is enough to pick a starting number and not enough to defend it. The slider surface exists so a human can correct it, and a human correction is a decision this file may never overwrite.

ring-dot.geometry: an annulus (r 34% / 29%) around a centred disc, r = 9%

period.measuredOn: shares dot-grid's measurement — same lattice, different mark

pinstripe-diagonal.geometry: a 45-degree band, 26% duty, corner to corner (tiles seamlessly)

period.method: not measured — a fine stripe field is below the resolution the available imagery can settle, and 26 is a starting number for the slider, declared as such rather than dressed up
period.caveat: UNMEASURED. AGENTS.md F5: a measurement without a corpus size is an opinion, so this one says n = 0 out loud.

crosshatch.geometry: two orthogonal bars, 16% wide, edge to edge

$doc: Tiles that EXIST and that no row keys yet, each with the reason it is still unkeyed.
A shipped tile nothing can reach is neither a bug nor an achievement: it is a drawn asset waiting for the
evidence that says where it belongs. Left unrecorded it goes one of two ways, and both are bad — somebody
deletes it as dead weight, or somebody keys it to an era on a hunch, which is the drawn-from-nothing defect
this tier exists to end. So it is declared here, and tools/build-ink-index.mjs cross-checks the declaration
against the rows in BOTH directions: a tile that is neither reachable nor listed fails the build, and a tile
listed here that a row has since started using fails it too, so the list cannot go stale in either direction.
unkeyedTiles.ring-dot: The mark the reverse-sheet recipe drew procedurally (an annulus around a centred dot), authored as a real tile so the design tier can replace the guess. No era or set in holo-archive/3b-pairs is measured as carrying THIS mark rather than a plain dot — 3b's pairs settle the delta CLASS, not the glyph — and keying it on the resemblance between our own fallback and our own tile would be circular. Waiting on a measurement of a specific reverse.
unkeyedTiles.pinstripe-diagonal: A fine 45-degree stripe field. 3b records fine-stripe reverses in the EX Plain block but explicitly cannot settle a stripe period from the available imagery (period.n is 0 for exactly that reason), and the EX rows that would carry it are the ones queued on `ex-set-logos`, a positioned stamp this lattice model cannot express. Keyed the day either half is resolved.

queued.usedBy: sv08.5 / sv10.5b / sv10.5w / me02.5 / sve reverse-foil-pokeball; BW-SV Trainer-card reverses
queued.why: A traced Poke Ball is TPCi's design and cannot enter a CC0 corpus. Ships as an ORIGINAL geometric recreation with its own notice section, or not at all.
queued.fallback: slot empty -> uInkOn 0 -> the recipe's procedural stand-in, exactly today's render

queued.mark: Love Ball, Quick Ball, Friend Ball, Dusk Ball
queued.why: Four more marks, same rule. Ascended Heroes is the set that proves variantKind belongs in the key: six distinct reverses of the same Pokemon on one sheet.

queued.usedBy: bw8 / bw9 / bw10 — Team Plasma cards only; the rest of each set takes the standard BW energy-symbol reverse
queued.why: Same rule. Additionally UNRESOLVED at the data level: the catalog declares one `reverse` kind for these sets, so which printings are Team Plasma cards is not expressible today and the row below cannot be written honestly yet.
queued.fallback: no row at all — bw8/9/10 resolve through the black-white era row

queued.usedBy: every Energy Pattern era: BW Emerging Powers -> SV. 3b: '~13 tiles per group', keyed on the Pokemon's type.
queued.why: Same rule, eleven times over. This is the largest queued item by printings governed and the one where `type` in the key finally does work.

queued.usedBy: ex7, ex8, ex9, ex10, ex11, ex12, ex13, ex14, ex15, ex16 — stamped INSIDE the art box, bottom right, every card
queued.why: Authored rasters, one per set, and per-language on top of that. Not a lattice at all: a single positioned stamp, so it needs the second small positioned layer 3b names in its section 4.2 rather than a tile. Recorded here so it is not lost; it is not a tile this schema can express.
queued.fallback: no row — the ten sets resolve through their era row

rows.note: The modern default: foil covers the body, not the art window, and the design is a staggered field over it. 3b classes every era from Diamond & Pearl onward as `frame` on the scan-diff axis.
Same shape as modern-sv. era-layouts.json already flags the swsh rects as an approximation borrowed from sv; this row inherits that weakness rather than hiding it.

e-Card Mirror reverses. 3b: `frame` on the scan-diff axis, with a real bottom-band ink swap (a 13-vertical-line strip replacing the e-Reader dot-code strip) that this lattice model does not express and that a positioned layer will have to.

Prismatic Evolutions, reverse #2 of 3. `null` delta class: the SCAN is identical for all three — TCGdex serves one image per card — and only the pattern assignment differs. That is exactly why this cannot be keyed on (era, type).
Prismatic Evolutions, reverse #3 of 3. Same sheet, same scan, different mark.

Ascended Heroes. SIX reverse kinds on one sheet (these five plus the plain `reverse`), which is the strongest single argument in the corpus for variantKind belonging in the key. One row, five kinds, one queued tile family — the schema absorbs it without five rows.

Legendary Collection, the TCG's first reverse set. `full` on the scan-diff axis (Fireworks over the entire face at every rarity) and `null` on the INK axis — the artwork ink is unchanged. So it needs no ink tile at all, and `noInk` records that as a DECISION rather than as an unfilled row: the resolver answers state 'no-ink', never 'queued', because nobody is waiting on a drawing here. strength 0 makes the same statement to the shader. 3b's warning applies: this set's class flipped between 1x and 3x zoom, which is why a card-scale eyeball is not a measurement.

EX Deoxys: the wheel pattern crosses the art window at EVERY rarity including commons, plus an 'ex DEOXYS' logo stamped inside the art box. One of the six `full`-class sets. The logo is a positioned stamp, not a lattice, and is queued as such.

EX Delta Species, RARITY-GATED. Rare and Holo Rare reverses get gold name, gold HP, a silver rarity symbol and (Holo Rare) gold borders; the Uncommon reverse gets none of it. This row exists to prove rarity is in the key — it is the axis (scope, type, variantKind) alone cannot express, and 3b section 4.4 names it as a model-breaker. Crystal Guardians goes further and gates on three named CARDS, which the `cards` field is here for. The gate matches a WHOLE rarity, never a substring: `rare` as a substring is true of 'Ultra Rare', 'Secret Rare', 'Radiant Rare', 'ACE SPEC Rare' and eleven more strings this catalog carries, and a gate that claims nearly everything proves nothing. Spelling variants are therefore listed EXPLICITLY — this catalog writes both 'Holo Rare' (lc) and 'Rare Holo' (base1) — because a list is reviewable and a fuzzy match is not.
